info.name: RCB Admin UI APIs Automation
info.description:
Every route of the **admin API** (`adminapis.rcbmatka.com`), the backend of the admin console (`master.rcbmatka.com`).

The folders follow the console's own menu: **deck › group › page**, for example **Treasury › Deposits › Pending**. Each page folder holds the requests that page sends. Its description names the console route and the component file, and lists the requests the page also uses from other folders. Detail pages, such as **Player Ledger**, sit next to the page they open from (`Approved › Player Ledger`).

## Start here

1. Pick an environment (top right): **RCB Matka · LIVE** or **RCB Matka · LOCAL**.
2. Open **Sign in (start here)** and send **Sign in as admin**. The token is saved in `{{admin_token}}`, and every request in this collection sends it as `Authorization: Bearer {{admin_token}}` (set on the collection).
3. Send anything else. Requests that need an id from an earlier request (a deposit, a withdrawal, a market, a chat…) get it from that request's saved variable, so run a page's list request before its actions.

To act as the **sub-admin**, send **Sign in as sub-admin**: its token replaces the admin's. **Go back to the tech admin** puts the tech admin's token back. A sub-admin gets `403` on pages their role does not have.

## Base URLs

| Variable | LIVE | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{admin_api}}` | `https://adminapis.rcbmatka.com/api` | every `/api/...` route |
| `{{admin_root}}` | `https://adminapis.rcbmatka.com` | the support-chat routes (`/chat-…`, `/chat-monitor/…`), `/health`, `/uploads/…` |
| `{{payment_url}}` | `https://payment.rcbmatka.com` | the two payout calls on **Treasury › Withdrawals › Pre-Approved**, and the UTR screenshots |

## Writes are switched off on LIVE

Every request that changes data (creates, edits, approves, declares, pays, sends) checks the environment's `allow_writes` first. When it is not `true` (LIVE ships with `false`), the request is **not sent** and the Console says why. Set `allow_writes` to `true` only while you mean to change live data, and set it back after.

Requests that **move money** say **Moves money** at the end of their description: wallet credits and debits, deposit and withdrawal decisions, payouts, result declarations and reverts, bid edits and voids, bonus voids, rate changes.

⚠️ Never use **Run collection** on LIVE with `allow_writes` set to `true`. A run declares and reverts results, approves and rejects money, changes settings and deletes notices, one request after another.

## Reading the answers

Most routes answer **HTTP 200** even when they refuse: the body carries `success` (`"1"` done, `"0"`/`"2"`/`"4"` refused or not found) and a `message`. Each request's tests check the HTTP status and save the values later requests need; read the body to see whether it did what you asked. Each request's description lists the fields the code reads, what it returns, its permission ids (a `tech_admin` always passes) and what it changes, including the audit-log action name.

## Variables this collection saves

Ids saved by one request and used by the next live in the collection's variables: `market_id`, `deposit_id`, `withdraw_order_id`, `bank_account_id`, `chat_ticket_id`, `desk_result_id`, `payin_setting_id` and others. Each variable's description says which request sets it. The sign-in values (`admin_token`, `tech_admin_token`, `sub_admin_token`, `admin_id`, `subadmin_id`) and the ids other collections share (`withdraw_order_id`, `deposit_image`, `deposit_order_id`, `market_id`, `starline_market_id`, `jackpot_market_id`) live in the environment.

## Where this comes from

Made from the route files (`app/routes/user.routes.js`, `app/routes/supportChat.routes.js`), the controllers, and the console's pages (`AdminCode/src/Layout/menuData.jsx` for the menu). It covers every route the server registers. Routes no console page calls any more are under **Not on a console page**. `GET /api/admin-profile` is registered twice; Express only runs the first.

It is generated by `postman/tools/build` and checked by `postman/tools/verify`, which runs every request against local copies of the services. See `postman/README.md`.

item.name: Sign in (start here)
Check the admin API is up · health

request.description:
Answers `ok` once the process is up: the liveness / readiness probe and load-balancer check. It is registered before the database connects and never touches MongoDB, so it says nothing about the database. The console does not call it.

**Who:** anyone, no token.

**Fields:** none.

**Returns:** 200 text/plain `ok`.

---
`GET /health`  
Code: `adminapis.rcbmatka.com/server.js:40 (app.get /health)`

Signs in a console account, as the console's sign-in page does (/login, User/Login.jsx), and saves its token. Use the tech admin here. One session per admin: each sign-in makes a new token and ends that admin's previous one (a console tab signed in as the same admin is signed out).

**Who:** anyone, no token.

**Fields:**
- `email` (string, required): the admin's email, trimmed, matched exactly; the account must be `active`.
- `password` (string, required): checked against the stored bcrypt hash (a password still in plain text is hashed on this sign-in).

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Login Successfully', token, usertype, psd}`: `usertype` is the role (tech_admin, admin or sub_admin), `psd` the session stamp the console compares with 'Who am I'. The answer has no `_id`: 'Who am I' saves admin_id (it is also `id` in the token's payload). Refusals are 200 too: `success:'4'` 'Enter your email and password.'; `success:'3'` 'Admin Not Exists Or Inactive. Please Check Again.' or 'Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.' (8 misses per email, or 30 per address, in 15 minutes). 500 `{success:'0', message:'Server error'}`.

Marked writes:false so a read-only run can sign in, but it does write admin.token (and the hash of a plain-text password).

---
`POST /api/login`  
Console page: `/login`  
Code: `adminapis.rcbmatka.com/app/controllers/admin.controller.js:136 (login)`

request.description:
The signed-in admin's own row. The console reads it on every page load (App.js: the role and `_id`, then the page permissions) and in the topbar (Layout/Header.jsx: the session-stamp check that signs out a tab whose password changed, and the avatar). Saves `data._id` into admin_id: the admin whose token is in admin_token (the sub-admin, right after 'Sign in as sub-admin').

GET /api/admin-profile is registered twice in user.routes.js (lines 176 and 574). Express only ever runs the first, admin.admin_profile; the second (admin.adminProfile, the same answer) is dead.

**Who:** any signed-in admin.

**Fields:** none.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully', data:{_id, email, roles, status, FullName, admin_id, ... (the admin row without password and token), avatar, session_stamp, password}}`: `password` repeats the session stamp for older console builds (never the password), `avatar` is the seed of their chip or card. 401 `{message:'Invalid Token'}` when the token is not that admin's current session.

Side effect: at most every 10 minutes it recomputes the players' colour bands in the background (users.color, from Colour Settings).

request.description:
Keeps a new chip or card as the signed-in admin's topbar avatar ('Deal me another' in the profile menu, Layout/Header.jsx).

**Who:** any signed-in admin; only their own.

**Fields:**
- `seed` (integer, required): 0 to 2147483647; the console sends a new random one. `null` goes back to the one worked out from their _id. A string or a decimal is refused.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully', avatar}` (the seed now in force); 200 `{success:'4', message:'Unknown avatar'}`; 200 `{success:'2', message:'Not Found'}`; 500 `{success:'0', message:'Server error'}`.

**Changes:** admin.avatar_seed.

---
`POST /api/admin-avatar`  
Console page: `every page`  
Permission: any signed-in admin  
Changes data: yes, so it is sent only when `allow_writes` is `true`  
Code: `adminapis.rcbmatka.com/app/controllers/admin.controller.js:439 (admin_avatar)`

exec: // This request changes data. It is sent only when allow_writes is "true" in the
// selected environment (LOCAL: true; LIVE: false until you set it to true).
console.warn('[RCB] Not sent: "' + pm.info.requestName + '" changes data, and allow_writes is not "true" in this environment.');

request.description:
Changes the signed-in admin's own password (the topbar's change-password modal sends `id:'self'`). The Roles pages use the same route with a sub-admin's _id and no old password. This request sets the tech admin's password again, unchanged (old = new = admin_password); signed in as the sub-admin, put subadmin_password in both, or the answer is 'Old password is incorrect'.

**Who:** any signed-in admin for their own (with the old password). Someone else's: a tech admin for any admin or sub-admin (not another tech admin), an admin for the sub-admins they created.

**Fields:**
- `id` (string, required): `self` (or their own _id), or the target admin's _id.
- `old_password` (string, required for their own): checked on the server.
- `password` (string, required): the new one, 8 to 72 bytes.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Password updated successfully', psd}` (`psd`, the new session stamp, for their own only). 200 `{success:'4'}` 'Old password is incorrect' or 'Use at least 8 characters for the password.'; 200 `{success:'2', message:'Not Found'}`; 403 `{success:'0', message:'You can only change the password of your own sub-admins.'}`.

**Changes:** admin.password (a new bcrypt hash) and password_changed_at; another admin's token is cleared (signed out). The new hash changes the session stamp, so the console signs this admin's open tabs out at their next profile check; the API token stays valid.

---
`POST /api/admin-update-password`  
Console page: `every page`, `/all_roles`, `/active_roles`, `/inactive_roles`  
Permission: any signed-in admin  
Changes data: yes, so it is sent only when `allow_writes` is `true`  
Code: `adminapis.rcbmatka.com/app/controllers/admin.controller.js:352 (admin_updatePassword)`

exec: // This request changes data. It is sent only when allow_writes is "true" in the
// selected environment (LOCAL: true; LIVE: false until you set it to true).
console.warn('[RCB] Not sent: "' + pm.info.requestName + '" changes data, and allow_writes is not "true" in this environment.');

var needed = {"admin_password":"Set it in the environment."};
if (!pm.variables.get(k)) console.warn('[RCB] {{' + k + '}} is empty.' + (needed[k] ? ' ' + needed[k] : ''));

request.description:
The pages an admin's role holds. The console reads its own on load (App.js, Dashboard.jsx, HomeDashboard.jsx; a tech admin skips it and gets every page) and the Roles pages read a sub-admin's (RolePermissionsModal.jsx). This request asks for the signed-in admin's own (admin_id, from 'Who am I').

**Who:** any signed-in admin for their own; another admin's: a tech admin, or an admin for the sub-admins they created.

**Fields:**
- `user_id` (string, required): the admin's _id.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully', data:[{_id, user_id, permissions:[{id, name, checked, children:[{id, name, checked}]}], updated_at}]}`; a page is granted when its `checked` is true. 200 `{success:'2', message:'No permissions assigned yet', data:[{user_id, permissions:[]}]}` (a tech admin usually has no row); 200 `{success:'4', message:'user_id is required', data:[]}`; 403 `{success:'0', message:'You can only see the pages of your own sub-admins.'}`; 500 `{error}`.

---
`POST /api/admin-permissions-list`  
Console page: `every page`, `/dashboard`, `/mobile-dashboard`, `/homedashboard`, `/all_roles`, `/active_roles`, `/inactive_roles`  
Permission: any signed-in admin  
Code: `adminapis.rcbmatka.com/app/controllers/admin.controller.js:577 (admin_permissions_list)`

request.description:
The same sign-in with the sub-admin's account, to see what a role with only some pages may do. Its token goes into admin_token, so every admin request you send after this one runs as the sub-admin, and into sub_admin_token. **Go back to the tech admin** (the last request of this folder) puts the tech admin's token back.

**Who:** anyone, no token.

**Fields:**
- `email` (string, required): the sub-admin's email.
- `password` (string, required): their password.

**Returns:** as 'Sign in as admin', with `usertype:'sub_admin'`. No `_id` in the answer, so subadmin_id is not saved here: run 'Who am I' next (it saves the sub-admin's _id into admin_id) or read `id` in the token's payload.

Writes the sub-admin's admin.token (ends their other session).

item.name: Go back to the tech admin · admin-profile

request.description:
Copies `tech_admin_token` (saved by **Sign in as admin**) back into `admin_token`, then reads the profile to show who the requests now run as. Use it after trying things as the sub-admin.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', data:{_id, email, roles:'tech_admin', ...}}`.

---

item.description:
Start here: check the API is up, sign in (saves admin_token and tech_admin_token), then 'Who am I' (saves admin_id). The console's sign-in page is /login (User/Login.jsx); the profile, avatar and password calls come from App.js and the topbar (Layout/Header.jsx) on every page.
'Sign in as sub-admin' replaces admin_token: every request after it runs as the sub-admin until 'Sign in as admin' is run again.

query.description: After how many minutes a withdrawal sent to the gateway counts as stuck: 5 to 1440, default 30. The console does not send it.

request.description:
Everything waiting on staff, as counts with a 5-row preview per bucket, in one read: the topbar's bell (Pages/Notifications/PendingActionsBell.jsx) asks every 45 s while the tab is visible.

**Who:** any signed-in admin; each bucket is sent only to roles holding its page (tech_admin gets them all).

**Fields:**
- `stalled_minutes` (query, optional, number): after how long a withdrawal at the gateway counts as stuck; 5 to 1440, default 30.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully', generated_at, stalled_minutes, total, urgent, buckets:[{id, title, note, severity, tone, href, action, count, amount?, oldest_at?, preview:[{id, primary, secondary, meta, at}], error?}], counts:{<bucket id>: n, withdrawals_on_wire}, degraded:[bucket ids]}`. Buckets: withdrawals_awaiting_review, withdrawals_awaiting_payout, withdrawals_wire_stalled, deposits_awaiting_approval, results_awaiting_declaration, results_due_soon, bank_accounts_awaiting_verification, player_chats_unanswered, ideas_awaiting_review. A bucket that fails reads 0 with `error:true`; 500 `{success:'0', message:'Could not read the pending-actions feed'}` only when the whole read fails.

---

Console page: `every page`  
Permission: any signed-in admin  
Code: `adminapis.rcbmatka.com/app/controllers/adminNotifications.controller.js:202 (pending_actions)`

item.name: Get the chat bubble count · chat-header-notification-count

request.description:
The topbar's chat bubble (Layout/Header.jsx, on load and every 30 s): the unread player messages and the newest unread chats for its pop-over. It lives under /api, unlike the other chat routes.

**Who:** any signed-in admin; staff without Player Chat (`adminchat`) or the Chat Monitor (`chat_monitor`, `chat_supervise`) get zeros. tech_admin always gets the counts.

**Fields:** none.

The house figures on the Control Deck, for today (the IST day) and all time. Each figure is counted with the query of the list its card opens (utils/dashboardFigures.js).

item.name: Send an announcement to one player · notification-store

request.description:
Puts an announcement in one player's in-app inbox (Notifications page, 'One player'; the page turns the picked username into a user_id with /api/user-list). It is not a push notification: nothing is sent to the phone, the app shows it in its inbox. No image: text only.

**Who:** admin token; page `notice_management` (tech_admin can always). The Notifications page itself is page `notification-list`, so a role with only that page gets 403 here.

**Fields:**
- `message` (string): the text. The console trims it and allows 300 characters; the API checks nothing (an empty or missing one is stored too).
- `user` (string, required): the player's user_id, not checked against the players: here the newest player, from 'List every player for a recipient picker' (put {{player_user_id}} to reach the test player). `all_user` sends to everyone (next request).

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully'}`: no orderid in the answer ('List sent announcements' shows it). 403 without the page; 500 `{error}`.

**Changes:** notifications: one row {message, orderid (24 random characters), type:'admin', status:'unseen', audience:'user', user_id, date:'DD-MM-YYYY hh:mm A', date_time:'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'} in IST. Audit action content.notification.

request.description:
The player roster, one page at a time, newest first, with every filter of All Players. All Players calls it on load and on Filter; Wallet Balances and the Treasury, Intel, Access and Notifications pages call it to look players up.
**Who:** admin token; no page permission (any signed-in admin). Mobile numbers come masked (`******0094`) unless a tech_admin is signed in.
**Fields** (query, all optional; the console sends every one, empty when unused):
- `page` number, default 1. `limit` number, default 10, max 200.
- `username`, `mobile`, `device_id`, `user_id`: partial, case-insensitive matches. `mobile` is matched on the full stored number, so masked viewers can search by it too.
- `min` / `max`: wallet balance (`credit`) in rupees. Both: between. Only `max`: up to. Only `min`: EXACTLY that balance (the dashboard's zero-balance link sends `min=0`).
- `status`: `active` | `inactive`. `color`: `red` | `orange` | `violet` | `yellow` | `blue` | `green`.
- `topwinnertoplosser`: `top_winner` (sort by win_amount) | `top_losser` (by loss_amount); otherwise newest first.
- `startDate` / `endDate`: `YYYY-MM-DD`, joined on or after / on or before that India day (`created_at`). Another format answers 500.
**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message, data:[players], pagination:{total, page, limit, totalPages}}`; no row carries password, password_copy, token, mpin or fcm_token. No match: 200 `{success:'2', message:'Not Found'}` with no data. `pagination.page` is null when `page` is not sent.
Saves the first row's `user_id` as `player_user_id_admin` and its `_id` as `player_doc_id` (the newest player when no filter is on). The player writes in this folder use `{{player_user_id}}` (the test player) instead.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message, data:{user_id, state, password}}`, where `state` is:
- `current`: `password` is the login password (checked against the bcrypt hash on every call);
- `outdated`: a copy exists but no longer logs in (`password` null);
- `unreadable`: the two APIs have different PLAYER_PASSWORD_KEY values (`password` null);

request.description:
One player's logins, newest first: Login History on All Players (`/login_history/:userid`) asks for that player's `user_id`, 10 a page. Live Sessions asks with no `user_id`, `limit=200` and `from` = the start of its window, for every login in the window.
**Who:** admin token; permission `login-user-list` (Live Sessions), `all_users`, `active_users` or `inactive_users` (tech_admin can always); without one, 403. The console's own `login_history` id is not accepted here. Mobiles come masked unless a tech_admin is signed in.
**Fields** (query, all optional):
- `user_id`: exact user_id; here `{{player_user_id}}`, the test player 9606710094 (set by the player sign-in). Without it: every player's logins.
- `page` default 1; `limit` default 10, max 200.
- `from`: a date or ISO date-time; only logins at or after it (Live Sessions sends e.g. 2026-10-21T08:00:00.000Z). An unparseable value is ignored.
- `device_id`: partial, case-insensitive match on the phone's device_id.
**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message, data:[logins], pagination:{total, page, limit, totalPages}}`; none: 200 `{success:'2', message:'Not Found'}` with no pagination; 500 `{error}`.
**Data** (one row per login, refused ones included; there are no logout rows): `user_id`, `username`, `mobile`; `ip` (the address the login came from); `state` (the Indian state the app reported); `lat` / `long` (the phone's coordinates, '0' when unknown); `device_id` (the app's build string of the phone: build id, board, brand, model...); `device_uid` (the phone's own Android id, app builds from 2026-10-09); `device_info` (model, Android and APK version text, 'Not provided', or 'BLOCKED:<reason>' for a login the geo/IP gate refused); `created_at`.

item.name: Create Player

request.description:
Creates a player account. The app has no sign-up screen: the player taps Register on WhatsApp, an agent does the KYC in the chat (nothing from it is stored), creates the account here on Create Player (`/create_user`), then sends the mobile number and password on WhatsApp by hand. The account is active at once; the joining bonus is decided at its first login.
**Who:** admin token; permission `create_user`, `all_users`, `active_users` or `inactive_users` (tech_admin can always); without one, 403.
**Fields** (no other keys are allowed):
- `username` string, required: the player's name. The console allows letters and spaces only; the API takes any text (here the obviously fake postman_test_player).
- `mobile` string (a JSON number is refused), required: the 10-digit login number, not already used. Here the fake 9000000001.
- `password` string, required, at least 6 characters (the console caps it at 20).
- `referral_code` string, optional, '' for none: a friend's code, checked before the account is made; case and symbols are ignored.
**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'User Add Successfully'}` (plus 'Linked to referral code X.' when one is linked); the answer has no user_id. 200 `{success:'4', message}`: a validation message, 'Password must be at least 6 characters long', 'Username already exists' (every run after the first), 'Mobile number already exists', 'Referral code X does not exist or is not active.', or referrals switched off. 500 `{success:'0', message:'Server error', error}`.
**Changes:** a REAL `users` row: random 24-character `user_id`, `app_id` rcbmatka, `status` active, `registered_by` admin, the bcrypt `password` and the sealed `password_copy` (shown in All Players); with a code, the referral link (bonusEngine.attachReferral). item.name: Live Sessions
Show who shares a phone or network · login-connections

query.description: 15m | 1h | 6h | 24h | 7d | 30d (default 24h)

request.description:
Live Sessions' Connections board: groups the logins of a time window by what accounts share, and joins phone and IP links into linked accounts (possible multi-accounting). Live Sessions calls it with its window, every 30 s while the tab is in front.
**Who:** admin token; permission `login-user-list` (Live Sessions), `all_users`, `active_users` or `inactive_users` (tech_admin can always); without one, 403. Mobiles come masked unless a tech_admin is signed in.
**Fields** (query):
- `window` optional: `15m` | `1h` | `6h` | `24h` (default) | `7d` | `30d`; anything else is read as 24h (and echoed back as sent).
**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully', data:{window, since, rows, capped, summary:{phones, ips, weak, rings, players_linked}, groups, rings}}`; 500 `{success:'0', message}`.
- `groups` (at most 300, strongest first), only keys shared by 2 or more players: `{id:'kind|key', kind, key, label, strength, logins, first_at, last_at, players:[{user_id, username, mobile, status, logins, last_at, last_ip, last_state, logins_here, last_here}]}`.
- `kind`: `phone` = the same handset (`device_uid`, the phone's Android id; strong); `ip` = the same public IP, e.g. a home or shop Wi-Fi (medium); `model` = the same `device_id` build string from older app builds, shared by identical phones (weak); `network` = a carrier (100.64.0.0/10) or private address (weak).
- `rings` (at most 300): players joined by phone or public-IP links, `{id, players, links:[{id, kind, key, label, players}], phones, ips, last_at}`.
- `rows` = logins read (up to 50,000; `capped` is true at the cap). `last_ip` / `last_state` are the address and Indian state of the player's latest login. Logins the geo/IP gate refused (device_info 'BLOCKED:...') are left out.

---
`GET /api/login-connections`

Permission: `login-user-list` or `all_users` or `active_users` or `inactive_users` (a tech_admin always passes)

request.description:
Creates a staff account: Create Sub Admin (`/create_roles`). Who may create what: a tech_admin an `admin` or a `sub_admin` (the console offers a tech_admin only Admin), an admin only a `sub_admin`, a sub_admin nothing.
**Who:** admin token; permission `create_roles`, `all_roles`, `active_roles` or `inactive_roles` (tech_admin can always); without one the API answers 403.
**Fields:**
- `email` string, required: a valid email (trimmed, case kept); it is the sign-in name and must not exist yet.
- `password` string, required: at least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes (stored as a bcrypt hash).

Saves the pages a staff account may open: Assign pages (RolePermissionsModal.jsx) on All Sub Admins, Active Roles and Inactive Roles sends the whole tree.
**Who:** admin token; permission `create_roles`, `all_roles`, `active_roles` or `inactive_roles` (tech_admin can always); without one the API answers 403. A tech_admin may set any admin's or sub-admin's pages, an admin only their own sub-admins'; nobody their own.
**Fields:**
- `user_id` string, required: the account's `_id`. Here `{{created_admin_id}}`, which no request sets (admin-create does not return the new _id): copy it from List my sub-admins. While it is empty the API answers 'user_id is required'.
- `permissions` array, required: the tree permissionCatalog.js `toSaved()` writes: groups `{id, name, checked, children:[{id, name, checked}]}`, a group `checked` only when every child is. Child ids are the console's permission ids: App.js `permissionRouteMap` turns each ticked id into the routes the console opens (`all_users` -> /all_users, `login-user-list` -> /user/login-user-list), and the API's requirePermission accepts an id ticked anywhere in the tree. `name` is only a label. The example gives the dashboard, All Players and Live Sessions.
- A non-tech admin can give only pages they hold: the others are saved unticked (clampTree).
**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully'}`; 200 `{success:'4', message:'user_id is required'}` or 'permissions must be an array'; 200 `{success:'2', message:'Not Found'}`; 403 `{success:'0', message:'You can only change the pages of your own sub-admins.'}`; 500 `{error}`.
**Changes:** upserts the account's `admin_permissions` row `{user_id, permissions, updated_at}`. When the account is an `admin`, each of their sub-admins keeps only the pages the admin still holds. Audit `admin.permissions`. The account sees the new pages at its next console load.

item.name: Approve a deposit and credit the player · deposit-status-update

request.description:
Take it in: marks one pending deposit success and credits the player's wallet. The Pending page's Take it in button.

**Who:** admin token; permission deposite_pending (tech_admin can always).

**Fields:**
- `id` string, required: the deposit's _id.
- `status` string, required: `success` here (Reject a deposit sends `reject`); anything else is refused with success '4'.
- `settlement_method` (or `settled_via`) string, optional: how it was settled, written on the row: manual | gateway | gateway_callback | gateway_status_check | auto_refund | unspecified (the default when absent or unknown); hand, by_hand and manually mean manual, wire and pg mean gateway. The console sends manual.
- `settlement_note` string, optional: replaces the settlement note the API writes on the row. Default for manual: Approved by an admin against UTR <utr>.
- `reason` string, optional: stored on the row when sent.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Update Successfully'}`. Refusals are 200 too: success '4' (bad status); success '2' with `Deposit request not found`, `Player <user_id> was not found, so the deposit can't be credited. Nothing was changed.` or `This deposit is already <status>. No change was made.` (only a pending row is settled, so a double click, or a PG callback that got there first, credits once). 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}` without the permission.

**Changes:** in one transaction: deposit_requests status success, settled_via/by/by_email/at/source, settlement_note and a settlement_events entry; users credit +amount, total_deposit +amount, total_count_deposit +1; a Passbook (wallets) row type deposit, remark Deposit Amount, action_by User, deposit_id. Then bonusEngine.settleUser (a deposit of the unlock amount releases the player's locked bonuses, each with its own Passbook row, and can pay their referrer); an inbox entry 'Deposit added' (₹<amount> has been added to your wallet.); an FCM push, title 'Deposit', body 'Your deposit request processed successfully'. Audit: deposit.status.

item.name: Approved

request.description:
Approved deposits (status success), newest first, 10 a page, with totals over the whole filtered list. The Approved page calls it on load, on Filter and on each how chip.

**Who:** admin token; any signed-in admin (no page permission is checked).

**Fields:** all optional; text filters are 'contains', case-insensitive, at most 100 characters; an unknown choice is ignored (never a 500).
- `page` string or number: from 1. Always 10 a page (the console's `limit` and `user_id`, the admin, are ignored).
- `user_name`, `player_user_id`, `AccountNumber`: the player's name, the player's user_id, the row's account number.
- `min`, `max`: amount in rupees; min alone means at least min; swapped when reversed; '1,500' and '₹1500' read as 1500.
- `startDate`, `endDate` YYYY-MM-DD: whole IST days (an impossible date is ignored), on `date_field`: requested (created_at, the default) | settled (settled_at).
- `how`: manual | gateway | auto_refund | unrecorded | '' (all); also hand, by_hand, auto, not_recorded. The summary is counted without it.
- `settled_by`: the settling admin's email. `ref`: UTR, order_id, getwaytxnid or gateway_ref. `gateway`: gateway_name or getway_name ('pg' also finds rows stored under the provider's old name). `paid_via`: qr_code | bank_account | online.
- `status`: success only (it can narrow the list, never widen it).

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully', data:[rows with settled_via, settled_by, settled_by_email, settled_at, settled_source, gateway_ref, settlement_note, settlement_events], pagination, totalRecords, totalNumberPage, summary}`; 200 `{success:'2', message:'Not Found', summary}` when the page is empty. `summary` = `{count, amount, hand, gateway, auto, unrecorded (each {count, amount}), how, by_how}` over the whole filtered list; by_how is the split without `how`, which the chips show.

item.name: Rejected
List rejected and failed deposits · deposit-reject-list

request.description:
Refused deposits, newest first, 10 a page: pushed back by an admin (status reject) and failed at PG (status fail, set by the payin callback). The Rejected page calls it on load, on Filter and on each how chip.

**Who:** admin token; any signed-in admin (no page permission is checked).

**Fields:** all optional; text filters are 'contains', case-insensitive, at most 100 characters; an unknown choice is ignored (never a 500).
- `page` string or number: from 1. Always 10 a page (the console's `limit` and `user_id`, the admin, are ignored).
- `user_name`, `player_user_id`, `AccountNumber`: the player's name, the player's user_id, the row's account number.
- `min`, `max`: amount in rupees; min alone means at least min; swapped when reversed; '1,500' and '₹1500' read as 1500.
- `startDate`, `endDate` YYYY-MM-DD: whole IST days (an impossible date is ignored), on `date_field`: requested (created_at, the default) | settled (settled_at).
- `how`: manual | gateway | auto_refund | unrecorded | '' (all); also hand, by_hand, auto, not_recorded. The summary is counted without it.
- `settled_by`: the settling admin's email. `ref`: UTR, order_id, getwaytxnid or gateway_ref. `gateway`: gateway_name or getway_name ('pg' also finds rows stored under the provider's old name). `paid_via`: qr_code | bank_account | online.
- `status`: reject | fail narrows to one kind of refusal (the dashboard's Today Rejected link sends reject); anything else is ignored.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Successfully', data:[rows with settled_via, settled_by, settled_by_email, settled_at, settled_source, gateway_ref, settlement_note, settlement_events], pagination, totalRecords, totalNumberPage, summary}`; 200 `{success:'2', message:'Not Found', summary}` when the page is empty. `summary` = `{count, amount, hand, gateway, auto, unrecorded (each {count, amount}), how, by_how}` over the whole filtered list; by_how is the split without `how`, which the chips show.

---
`POST /api/deposit-reject-list`

Permission: any signed-in admin

item.name: Send the payout to the bank through PG · payout/index.php

query.description: The withdrawal's 14-digit orderid (only letters, digits, _ and - are kept).

request.description:
Send on the wire: the payment service sends one pre-approved withdrawal to the player's bank by IMPS through PG. Only the order id travels; amount, account, IFSC and holder come from the withdrawal row. The Pre-Approved page calls it after a confirm, with a 30 s timeout.

**Who:** the admin Bearer token, checked by the payment service: HS256 with ADMIN_JWT_SECRET (it must equal the admin API's secret), not expired, an active admin, and the session saved at their last login. CORS answers only the console's origin (ADMIN_CONSOLE_ORIGINS). Permission withdrawal_pending_Approve or withdrawal_pending (tech_admin can always).

**Fields:**
- query `orderid` string, required: the row must be pending, admin_approve yes, never sent (no getwayorderid) and not being sent by another request.

**Returns:** JSON with `status` true or false, HTTP 200 unless noted:
- `{status:true, message:'pending', gateway_status:'INITIATED', transfer_id, in_flight:true}`: accepted, now at the bank (the normal answer); `{status:true, message:'Success'}`: settled at once.
- `{status:false, message, auto_reject:true, refunded, gateway_status}`: the bank declined it; it is already rejected and refunded (`refunded:false` with a retry message when the refund could not be written yet).
- `{status:false, message}`: `Missing orderid`; `Withdrawal not found for this order id`; `This withdrawal is already <status>. Nothing was sent.`; not approved yet; already sent (use Check Status); being sent right now; `Cannot pay out: <field> is missing...`; PG unreachable (not sent) or no answer (may have been sent); an unreadable (+ http_code) or undecryptable answer; a duplicate order id; an unexpected gateway status (+ gateway_status); PG's own refusal (+ gateway:{status, http_code}).
- 401 `{status:false, message:'Sign in to the admin console again.'}` (or session expired / ended / admin not active); 403 `You do not have permission to send payouts.`; 503 when ADMIN_JWT_SECRET is not set.

**Changes:** claims the row (payout_sending_at/by) and calls PG. In flight: getwayorderid, gateway_name pg, gateway_status, a settlement_events entry, the status sweep armed. Settled: status success, utr, settled_via gateway, users total_withdraw/total_count_withdraw. Declined: in one transaction status reject, reason, users.credit refund and a Passbook row type deposit, remark Withdraw Request Rejected Amount Refund, action_by System. No push or inbox entry. Logged in logs/api.log.

item.name: Check the payout at PG · payout/checkstatus.php

query.description: The withdrawal's orderid. The row only has to exist (any status).

request.description:
Check the wire: asks PG what happened to one payout and applies the answer. The same logic as the PG webhook and the status sweep (payout_status_lib.php), so a refund happens only once whoever gets there first. The Pre-Approved page's Check the wire button.

**Who:** the admin Bearer token, checked by the payment service: HS256 with ADMIN_JWT_SECRET (it must equal the admin API's secret), not expired, an active admin, and the session saved at their last login. CORS answers only the console's origin (ADMIN_CONSOLE_ORIGINS). Permission withdrawal_pending_Approve, withdrawal_pending, withdrawal_complete or withdrawal_reject (tech_admin can always).

**Fields:**
- query `orderid` string, required: the withdrawal's orderid.

**Returns:** HTTP 200 unless noted:
- `{status, message, state, gateway_status, auto_reject, refunded, settled_via, settled_by, settled_source:'payout/checkstatus.php', gateway_name:'pg', gateway_ref, utr}`; `state` settled (status true, `The gateway has settled this payout.`), declined (auto_reject true: rejected and refunded now, or already settled so nothing changed), in_flight (`The bank has not settled this one yet. Check again in a few minutes.`) or unknown (an unexpected PG status).
- `{status:false, message, http_code}` when PG could not be asked (unreachable, unreadable, internal error, not OK, undecryptable).
- `{status:false, message:'Missing orderid'}` or `Withdrawal not found for this order id`; 401, 403 (`You do not have permission to check payouts.`), 503 as for the payout.

**Changes:** settled (from pending): status success, getwayorderid, utr, settled_via gateway_status_check, users total_withdraw/total_count_withdraw. Declined (from pending): status reject, reason, users.credit refund and a Passbook row type deposit, remark Withdraw Request Rejected Amount Refund, action_by System, in one transaction. In flight: getwayorderid when missing, gateway_status. Every answer appends a settlement_events entry. No push or inbox entry.

item.name: Mark a withdrawal paid by hand · withdraw-status-update

request.description:
Acts on `{{withdraw_order_id_2}}`, the **second** pre-approved withdrawal (the first is the one sent through PG above).

Settle by hand: records a withdrawal as paid in our own books. It sends no money: use it only when the player was paid another way. The Pre-Approved page sends the row's orderid as `id`.

**Who:** admin token; permission withdrawal_pending or withdrawal_pending_Approve (tech_admin can always).

**Fields:**
- `id` string, required: the 14-digit orderid (what the console sends) or the Mongo _id.
- `status` string, required: `success` here (Reject a withdrawal sends `reject`); anything else is refused with success '4'.
- `settlement_method` (or `settled_via`) string, optional: how it was settled, written on the row: manual | gateway | gateway_callback | gateway_status_check | auto_refund | unspecified (the default when absent or unknown); hand, by_hand and manually mean manual, wire and pg mean gateway. The console sends manual.
- `settlement_note` string, optional: replaces the settlement note the API writes on the row.
- `reason` string, optional: stored on the row (null when not sent).

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Update Successfully'}`; 200 success '2' with `Withdraw request not found`, `This withdrawal is being sent to the bank right now, so it can't be settled by hand...` or `This withdrawal is already <status>. No change was made.`; 200 success '4' (bad status); 403 without the permission.

**Changes:** only from pending and not while a PG send is under way (2 minutes): withdraw_requests status success, reason, settled_* fields and a settlement_events entry; users total_withdraw +amount and total_count_withdraw +1 (the wallet is not touched, the amount left it when the player asked; no Passbook row). An inbox entry 'Withdrawal paid' (Your withdrawal of ₹<amount> has been processed.) and an FCM push, title 'Withdraw', body 'Your withdrawal request processed successfully'. - `reason` string: shown to the player in the inbox entry and stored on the row (the console requires one; the API does not).
- `settlement_method` (or `settled_via`) string, optional: how it was settled, written on the row: manual | gateway | gateway_callback | gateway_status_check | auto_refund | unspecified (the default when absent or unknown); hand, by_hand and manually mean manual, wire and pg mean gateway. The console sends manual.
- `settlement_note` string, optional: replaces the settlement note the API writes on the row.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Update Successfully'}`; 200 success '2' with `Withdraw request not found`, `This withdrawal was already sent to the bank (transfer <id>). It can't be rejected now: check its status instead...`, `Player <user_id> was not found, so the amount can't be returned. Nothing was changed.`, being sent right now, or `This withdrawal is already <status>. No change was made.`; 200 success '4' (bad status); 403 without the permission.

**Changes:** in one transaction, only from pending and never sent to PG: withdraw_requests status reject, reason, settled_* fields and a settlement_events entry; users.credit +amount; a Passbook (wallets) row type deposit, remark Deposit Amount Withdraw Request Reject, action_by User, withdraw_id. Then an inbox entry 'Withdrawal returned' (Your withdrawal of ₹<amount> was not processed and the amount is back in your wallet. Reason: <reason>) and an FCM push, title 'Withdraw', body 'Your withdrawal has been request rejected'. Audit: withdrawal.status.

item.name: Open a new main market board · add-market

request.description:
Creates a board (*Open the board* on the page). Its `market_id` is the name with every space removed. Main boards have both sessions. The example is a hidden test board (Show in app: no) late in the day, so it never becomes the first board in the lists; a second run answers "Market Name Already Exist".
**Who:** admin token with `main_market_list`: any Markets page passes the route, then the controller needs the page of the type being added (tech_admin can always).
**Fields** (all required; Joi refuses any other key):
- `market_type`: `mainmarket` | `kingstarline` | `kingjackport`.
- `market_name` (string): the name players see; must not equal an existing board's name or id (exact match, any type).
- `open_time`, `close_time` (HH:mm, 24-hour IST): when open bids and close bids stop; open before close. Starline/Jackpot: open fields "NA".
- `open_result_time`, `close_result_time` (HH:mm): each at or after its bid deadline; a close result earlier than the open result only 00:00–05:59 (after midnight).
- `close_before_minute` (digits as a string, e.g. "10"): the page's "Cut-off"; stored only, nothing enforces it (bidding stops at `open_time`/`close_time`). `show_in_app` ("yes" | "no"); `monday` … `sunday` (booleans).
**Returns:** 200 `{success:"1", message:"Market Add Successfully"}` (the new board's id is not returned: find it with the list); 200 `{success:"4", message}` for a missing field, bad hours or a duplicate ("Market Name Already Exist"); 403 `{success:"0", code:403, message}` without the type's page.
**Changes:** inserts a `market` document (app_id `rcbmatka`). Audit: `market.add`.

request.description:
Declares the open pana and settles every waiting open-session bid on the board for that day: winners are paid at their rate (stake × rate ÷ 10), losers recorded, bids that can't be settled refunded. Declaring the same number again only finishes anything left; a different number is refused until reverted.
**Who:** admin token with `declare_main` (tech_admin can always).
**Fields:**
- `session` (required): `open` | `close`.
- `market_id` (required): the board's market_id.
- `result_date` (required): DD-MM-YYYY as the page sends it (YYYY-MM-DD also accepted); not in the future. For today, refused until the session's bid deadline has passed (open: `open_time`, close: `close_time`).
- `result_number` (string, required): the pana, a real pana ("000"–"999").

What each game pays. A rate is what a ₹10 bid wins (settlement pays stake × rate ÷ 10), with the smallest and largest stake. Rates are stored as text.

The Arena deck of the console: market boards, Game Load (what the house is carrying), declaring results, the Result Desk (correcting results and bids) and payout rates.
Declares, reverts, voids, Result Desk changes and rate saves move real money (`writes` + `money`). The rules live in `app/utils/settlement.js`, `app/utils/gameRules.js` and `app/utils/resultDesk.js`.
Run order matters: *List main market boards*, *List King Starline boards* and *List King Jackpot boards* save the market ids every later folder uses.

request.description:
Saves App Setting fields; only the fields sent are written, and a missing or unknown `id` falls back to the one settings document. Every change is live for every player at once. The example writes back the copyright line read by 'Read the app settings', so nothing changes.

**Who:** Bearer admin token; permission `config` (tech_admin can always). Without it: 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}`.

**Fields** (body, all optional strings; any other key is ignored):
- `id`: the settings `_id`.
- `withdraw_enable_disable`: `yes`/`no`; `no` freezes every withdrawal (the player API refuses them; the website shows them closed).
- `withdraw_open_time`, `withdraw_close_time`: `HH:mm`, 24-hour IST; requests outside the window are refused (it may cross midnight).
- `min_withdraw`, `max_withdraw` (₹, `0` = no limit) and `per_day_withdraw_request` (requests per player per day; blank or `0` refuses every request): enforced by the player API unless the player has limits of their own.
- `withdraw_upi`: `true`/`false`; `false` = the app offers bank payouts only, `true` adds PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm.
- `min_deposit`, `max_deposit` (₹): used by the app's deposit screen and shown on the website.
- `deposit_on_off`: `on`/`off`; `off` makes the payment service refuse deposits and the app show them paused.
- `payinPaymentMode`: `online`/`offline` (the page's 'Deposit routing': gateway or manual queue); nothing in the player API, payment service or app reads it today.
- `apk_version`: the required app build number; an installed build below it gets a non-dismissible update sheet.
- `geo_restriction_enabled`: `1` = the state and IP gate is on, anything else off (normally set on Access → Allowed States).
- `home_screen_marquee`: the app's scrolling home banner. `home_screen_msg`, `copy_right`: stored; the app and website do not show them today.
- `mobile` (10 digits): the payment service texts deposit alerts to it; the website shows it. `email_id`, `telegram_link`: shown on the website.
- `application_name`, `company_address`, `playstore_link`, `youtube_link`: stored; the app and website do not show them today.

The model refuses a blank or other value for the enums `withdraw_upi`, `deposit_on_off`, `payinPaymentMode`. WhatsApp numbers (Contact Numbers) and bonus fields (Bonuses & Referrals) are ignored.

**Full-form save:** the page posts the whole document it loaded minus `_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `__v`, the WhatsApp/contact fields and the bonus fields, plus `id` = `_id`: every one of the 23 fields above that the document holds, at once, including `deposit_on_off` and `geo_restriction_enabled` as they were when the page loaded (no console page has a control for `deposit_on_off`; the geo switch lives on Allowed States).

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'App Setting updated successfully', data:{settings}, updated_fields:[…]}`; 200 `{success:'4', message}` for a bad enum value or 'Nothing to update'; 404 `{success:'2', message:'App Setting document does not exist yet'}`.

**Changes:** the `appSetting` document (the fields sent, and `updated_at`). Audit `settings.update`.

item.name: Add a WhatsApp or call number · contact-number-add

request.description:
Adds a WhatsApp number (for sign-ups, support or both) or a support call line. Adding a WhatsApp number that is already listed merges the roles, or switches it back on, instead of failing. The Contact Numbers page sends it from its add form. The example adds +44 7700 900001, a number reserved for fiction, as a sign-up number.

**Who:** Bearer admin token; permission `contact_numbers` or `config` (tech_admin can always). Without it: 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}`.

**Fields** (body):
- `channel` (required): `whatsapp` or `call`.
- `country_code` (string, digits, e.g. `91`): taken off the front of `number` if typed there too.
- `number` (string, required): the national number; anything but digits is dropped. India (`91`): 10 digits starting 6–9; otherwise 6–14 digits, at most 15 with the code.
- `role`: `onboarding`, `support` or `both` (WhatsApp; a call line is always support), or `roles:{onboarding, support}`.
- `label` (string, optional, 40 characters): whose phone it is.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Added +44 7700900001 for Onboarding.', id, data:{whatsapp:[row], call:[row], queues:{onboarding, support}, primary:{whatsapp, call}, legacy:{…}}}` (a merge adds `merged:true`); 200 `{success:'2', message:'… is already listed for …', data}`; 400 `{success:'0', message}` for a bad channel, number or role; 409 when the same number was added a moment ago. Saves `id` as `contact_number_id`.

**Changes:** inserts a `contact_numbers` row and rewrites the old App Settings fields (`whatsapp_Number`, `whatsapp_Number_first`, `support_numbers`, `onboarding_whatsapp`). An active number joins its rotation at once. Audit `settings.contacts`.

request.description:
Changes a number's digits, label, role or on/off status. The Contact Numbers page sends it from Save, the role buttons and the on/off switch, each with only the changed keys.

**Who:** Bearer admin token; permission `contact_numbers` or `config` (tech_admin can always). Without it: 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}`.

**Fields** (body; only the keys sent are changed):
- `id` (string, required): the number's `id` from the list.
- `country_code`, `number`: as in 'Add a WhatsApp or call number'; a number already listed on that channel → 409.
- `label` (40 characters); `role` (`onboarding`/`support`/`both`, WhatsApp only; a WhatsApp number must keep a role); `status` (`active` or `inactive`).

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Saved.' (+ what happens to its players), data:{listing}}`; 400 `{success:'0', message:'Which number? No id was given.' | 'Nothing to change.' | …}`; 404 `{success:'0', message:'That number no longer exists. Refresh the page.'}`; 409 on a clash.

**Changes:** updates the `contact_numbers` row and the old App Settings fields. Switching off a support number, or taking support off it, sends its players to the next support number on their next ask. Audit `settings.contacts`.

---
`POST /api/contact-number-update`  
Console page: `/contact_numbers`  
Permission: `contact_numbers` or `config` (a tech_admin always passes)  
Changes data: yes, so it is sent only when `allow_writes` is `true`  
Code: `adminapis.rcbmatka.com/app/controllers/contactNumber.controller.js:238 (update)`

item.name: Save the blocked-screen support setting · blocked-support-settings

request.description:
Saves the 'Support on blocked screens' setting; the player API applies it within 15 seconds. The example saves the defaults: the button on every kept-out screen, for all players, with each player's own support number.

**Who:** Bearer admin token; permission `contact_numbers` or `config` (tech_admin can always). Without it: 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}`.

**Fields** (body):
- `enabled` (boolean, required): the button at all.
- `screens` (array, required): any of `account` (blocked or inactive account), `region` (state not allowed), `network` (address not approved for the state), `ip_blocked` (address blocked by staff), `location` (GPS off or fake).
- `audience` (required): `all`, `only` (only the listed players) or `except` (everyone but them).
- `players` (array of `user_id`s, at most 500; required for `only`): each must be a real player.
- `number_id` (string, optional): the `id` of an active WhatsApp number from Contact Numbers; empty = the player's own support number.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Saved', data:{as 'Read the blocked-screen support setting'}}`; 400 `{success:'0', message:'Say whether the button is on or off' | 'Pick the screens from the list' | 'Pick who sees it: …' | 'Add the players who should see it' | 'No player with the id …' | 'That WhatsApp number is not on the list' | …}`.

**Changes:** `appSetting.blocked_support`. Audit `settings.blocked-support`.

Upload chart results from a CSV file · result-create-csv

request.description:
Imports chart results from a CSV file into `results`, without settling or paying anybody. The CSV Result Upload page posts the file as multipart.

**Who:** Bearer admin token; permission `upload-manul-results` or `upload_manul_results` or `upload-result-inCSV` or `upload_result_inCSV` (tech_admin can always). Without it: 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}`.

**Fields** (multipart): `resultCsv` (file, required): a `.csv` (type text/csv, text/plain, application/vnd.ms-excel or application/octet-stream), at most 5 MB. First line = the headers, exactly these names, comma-separated, no BOM:
- `marketId` (required): the market's `market_id` (not checked against the markets). `marketType` (required): stored as is; declarations write `mainMarket`, `kingstarline`, `kingjackport`.
- `date`: **MM-DD-YYYY**, the chart's format; stored as given, not validated.
- `dayOfResult` (e.g. `Mon`); `dateTimeResult` (free text; declarations write `DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm:ss`).
- `openDigit` (required) → `result`, the open pana; `jodiDigit` → `result2`, the jodi; `closeDigit` → `result3`, the close pana.

A row is skipped silently when a required column is empty, when that market and date already have a result, or when bids for that day are still waiting (checked only when `date` is a valid MM-DD-YYYY).

```
POSTMAN_TEST,mainMarket,01-04-2000,Tue,04-01-2000 13:00:00,250,79,379
```

request.description:
Lists IP rules across every state in one read, with counts per state, type and status, the state roster and the master switch, so the pages can say which rules are live. Allowed Addresses (type allow) and Blocked Addresses (type block) call it on load and on every filter; Allowed States calls it with `limit: 1` for the counts.

**Who:** Bearer admin token (any active admin); no page permission.

**Fields** (body, all optional):
- `type`: `allow` (every rule that is not a block) or `block`; anything else = both.
- `state`: an exact state name, or `*` for the universal rules; empty = all.
- `status`: `active` or `blocked` (`blocked` = the rule is switched off); empty = both.
- `q`: text found in ip, username, mobile, label or user_id (case-insensitive).

item.name: Add an IP rule for a state · ip-whitelist-add

request.description:
Adds an IP rule for one state: an allow rule (this player may use the app from this address while the state is in `whitelist` mode) or a block rule (`type: 'block'`: the address is refused in that state while the master switch is on). Allowed Addresses sends allow rules, Blocked Addresses per-state blocks. The example allows the test player from a documentation address (203.0.113.10), so real traffic is not affected.

**Who:** Bearer admin token; permission `geo_whitelist` (tech_admin can always). Without it: 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}`.

**Fields** (body):
- `state` (string, required): an exact state name. The API also takes `*`, which makes a universal rule.
- `ip` (string, required): one exact IPv4 or IPv6 address (no ranges; the API does not validate it).
- `type`: `block`, anything else = `allow`.
- `user_id`: the player's `user_id`; required for an allow rule, optional for a block (empty = everyone on that address).
- `username`, `mobile`, `label` (optional): shown in the tables.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Added', data:{_id, state, type, user_id, username, mobile, ip, label, status, created_at, updated_at}}`; 200 `{success:'0', message:'state and ip are required' | 'Pick a user for an allow rule' | 'This rule already exists'}`. Saves `data._id` as `whitelist_id`.

**Changes:** inserts an `ip_whitelist` row, read by the player API's gate. Audit `access.whitelist`.

item.name: Blocked Addresses
Block an IP address everywhere · ip-block-add

request.description:
Blocks an IP address everywhere: the player API refuses it on every request, login and registration included, in every state, even with the master switch off. Blocked Addresses sends it for an 'Everywhere' block; Live Sessions sends it to block a player's address. The example blocks a documentation address (203.0.113.50) that no real client uses; run again, it answers 'This IP is already blocked'.

**Who:** Bearer admin token; permission `geo_ip_block` (tech_admin can always). Without it: 403 `{success:'0', code:403, message}`. Editing or deleting the block needs `geo_whitelist` ('Edit or switch off an IP rule', 'Delete an IP rule').

**Fields** (body):
- `ip` (string, required): one exact address (not validated).
- `user_id` (string, optional): only this player is refused from the address; empty = everyone on it.
- `username`, `mobile`, `label` (optional): shown in the tables.

**Returns:** 200 `{success:'1', message:'Blocked', data:{_id, state:'*', type:'block', user_id, username, mobile, ip, label, status:'active', created_at, updated_at}}`; 200 `{success:'0', message:'ip is required' | 'This IP is already blocked'}`; 500 `{success:'0', message}`.
